topic.title: Leap Year Check
topic.description: Determines whether a year is a leap year using divisibility rules: divisible by 4, not by 100, unless also by 400. Teaches compound boolean expressions.

learningNotes.whatILearned: One line can hold the whole leap-year rule, as long as `and` and `or` are bracketed in the right order.
learningNotes.challenges: I wrote the rule with no brackets and no comment, and the precedence is doing the work by accident.
learningNotes.nextSteps: Bracket the two halves and say what each one means.

files.description: Leap year checker with compound boolean logic.

misconceptions: `and` binds tighter than `or`, so `a and b or c` means `(a and b) or c` — the rule works, but only by luck of precedence
The century rule has to be tested separately from the four-year rule; a leap year is every fourth year *except* centuries *except* every fourth century
engine.review:
**The rubric I used**

There is no task sheet for this one — it was written before the engine
existed, so there was nothing to grade it against. I graded the file on the
three things that have always mattered here:

- **40 — it runs.** It compiles or interprets without an error.
- **30 — it is right.** The output is what it claims to produce.
- **30 — it explains itself.** Comments say *why*, not *what*.

**40 + 30 + 0 = 70%**

**What is solid**

The rule is complete and correct. I checked both awkward years: 1900 prints *This is not a leap year* and 2000 prints *This is a leap year*. Those two are exactly the cases that separate the real rule from `year % 4 == 0`, so getting both right is the whole exercise.

**What is not**

The condition is `a%4==0 and a%100!=0 or a%400==0` with no brackets. It is correct, because `and` binds tighter than `or`, so Python reads it as `(a%4==0 and a%100!=0) or (a%400==0)` — but nothing in the file says that, and the next person to edit it will get it wrong. There is also no comment, and the condition *is* the lesson.

**The one thing to fix first**

```python
if (a % 4 == 0 and a % 100 != 0) or a % 400 == 0:  # every 4th, except centuries, except every 400th
```

Brackets for the reader, and the rule in words.
